### problem_chain

**Root problem.** "I want to know whether I am owed anything on it" — the allowance the schedule owed
for benefit periods already gone. That is `allowance_ext_schedule_catch_up_load`,
`computes: catch_up_amount`, `target_tool: post_catch_up_load_838eeda2` (`owner=agent`).

**Prerequisite sentence carried by the root's own rule** (one): *"The allowance owed for the benefit
periods already gone is not made available before the card stands in use on the programme record."*

**Edge → `allowance_ext_card_in_use_first_load`.** False at the opening:
`allowance_programs["7bc19e7a-…"]` stands at `status: "card_issued"` with `card_activated_date: ""`
and `current_balance: "0.00"`, and `initial_state` carries **no** `allowance_card_ledger` table at
all — the card has never been brought into use and nothing has ever been loaded. `kind: value_input`,
`gate: loads_made`. Resolved by `activate_allowance_card_a5740baf` (**`owner=user`**), which is the
only write of this difficulty that sets `card_activated_date` and moves the programme to `active`.
**Load-bearing:** skip it and replay — the catch-up computes to **0.00** instead of 408.34, because
`ledger_entries` stays 0 (so `current_index` = 0), `card_in_use` stays "" (so `last_period_index` =
−1) and `owed_total` = 116.67 + (−1 − 1) × 175.00 = −233.33, floored to nothing.

**Shape.** n = 1 prerequisite problem, `value_input` (1 ≥ max(n−1,1) = 1), no cycle, depth 2.
**Customer's own write:** `activate_allowance_card_a5740baf` is `owner=user` and the persona hands it
over passively — "If the representative explains that bringing the card into use is something only he
can do and hands it over to him, he does it there and then."

**No parallel edges**, so no competing terminal state. **No waiting:** the activation needs only the
last four digits, which the member reads out. **Base gate:** `activation_window_open` — the card was
posted `card_issued_date: 2026-09-04`, the Premier window is 120 days, so the last day is 2027-01-02;
today is 2026-10-20, in time. `card_activation_required` is true on Premier, so the member's act is
required rather than optional.

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** `activate_allowance_card_a5740baf` creates the load row and
updates the programme with no conditional and no status check; `post_catch_up_load_838eeda2` creates
the bonus-load row and updates the balance with no conditional. Neither inspects
`card_activated_date`, programme status or ledger history, and neither returns an error or a hint.

**`SOURCE-CHAIN RED` — the customer names the prerequisite.** The member's opening words are:
*"A card came with my plan papers back in September and I have not done a thing with it. **I would
like to be able to use it at the chemist**, and I want to know whether I am owed anything on it."*
The second clause is the root problem. The first is the prerequisite problem, stated in plain
business words: the lifecycle transition `card_issued → active` is defined in this very charter as
"The member activates the card and **the allowance becomes spendable**", and being able to use the
card at a chemist is precisely that state. He asks for it outright, in his first half-minute, before
the representative has read a single record — and the persona confirms he says it unprompted ("That
is the whole of what he wants, and he says it in the first half minute").
*Consequence:* the edge that this task exists to test is not tested. An agent that never reads the
prerequisite sentence — indeed an agent that reads no policy at all — still performs the activation,
because the customer asked for it; the derivation "the catch-up load cannot be made until the card
stands in use on the programme record" is never needed to reach the write order. The problem tree's
one hop is supplied by the persona rather than discovered from the policy, which is exactly what the
tree is meant to make the agent do. Contrast task 0, where the three prerequisites appear only as
reactions gated on the representative raising them first.
*Artifact:* `tasks/supplemental_benefit_allowance_desk/tasks/1.json` → `user_scenario`, paragraph 1;
against `allowance.extended.yaml` → `allowance_ext_schedule_catch_up_load` → `prerequisite[0]` →
`policy_source`.

**Isomorphism with the author's declared tree.** The tree derived here from the policy and the world
alone — root `allowance_ext_schedule_catch_up_load` with the single `value_input` prerequisite
`allowance_ext_card_in_use_first_load`, order 1 → 2 — is checked against `prerequisite_closure` after

**`SOURCE-TASK RED` — the catch-up load's `benefit_period` is not entailed.** The tool requires it
("Fixed-format class — the benefit period the extra load is placed in, written as a benefit period as
YYYY-Qn"), and no sentence of `allowance_ext_schedule_catch_up_load`'s rule says which period the
extra load is placed in. Its own compute never binds a period label. Base
`allowance_load_schedule`'s correcting-load sentence ("A load made short or made twice is put right
by a correcting load that names the load it corrects") fixes only which load it names, not which
period it sits in; base `allowance_rollover_and_expiry`'s "An allowance belongs to the benefit period
it was loaded for" pushes toward the period the allowance was owed for — but the 408.34 is the lump
of three of them (the Q2 share, the whole of Q3 and the whole of Q4). Three defensible readings sit
on the record: `2026-Q4` (the period it is made available in), `2026-Q2` (the first period the
allowance is owed for, which is where the base sentence points), and `2026-Q3` (the period of the
load it names). Nothing in the charter excludes two of the three. *Consequence:* a scored parameter
with three defensible values, and the choice is not cosmetic — a catch-up placed in `2026-Q2` or
`2026-Q3` would fall inside a period `allowance_ext_period_end_expiry` treats as already dying, and
one placed in `2026-Q4` would not. *Artifact:* `allowance.extended.yaml` →
`allowance_ext_schedule_catch_up_load` → `rule`, `compute`; `task_tools.py` →
`post_catch_up_load_838eeda2`, `benefit_period`.

**Contrasting number on the opening world.** Computed before the prerequisite is resolved, the same
policy gives **0.00**. The handling-time figure is the right one because the root's own prerequisite
sentence says the allowance "is not made available before the card stands in use on the programme
record", so the quantity is not defined until write 1 stands.

**Cap check.** Total loaded for the year becomes 58.33 + 408.34 = 466.67, inside Premier's
`annual_allowance_amount` of 700.00 and well inside the combined cap of 1400.00 in base
`allowance_agg_combined_annual_cap`.

**Terminal state.** Programme `7bc19e7a-…`: `status: active`, `card_activated_date: 2026-10-20`,
`card_number_last_four: 8802`, `current_balance: 466.67`; the ledger carries the activation load of
58.33 in `2026-Q3` and a `allowance_bonus_load` of 408.34 with `entry_reason: load_correction`
naming it.

**Write order:** verify identity → reads → write 1 (the member) → write 2 (the agent).

### factor_weight

Every figure below is this auditor's own recomputation on the handling-time world.

**Computation 1 — `first_load_amount` (gold 58.33), 4 factors, 2 `method` + 2 `parameter`.**

| factor | effect | tier taken (evidence) | baseline | scored under baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `first_load_months_covered` | method — which months are counted | tier 1: `current_index` 3 > `opening_index` 2 | `period_months` = 3 | **175.00** |
| `first_load_period_allowance` | parameter — a figure | tier 1: plan `active`, `otc_allowance_quarterly` 175.00 > 0 | 0.00 | **0.00** |
| `first_load_share_basis` | method — which formula | tier 1: prorating tier, `months_into_opening_period` 2 ≥ 1 | 0.00 | **0.00** |
| `first_load_ceiling` | parameter — a figure | tier 1: yearly allowance 700.00, no load yet | 0.00 | **0.00** |

All four change the scored value under baseline substitution. Whole-baseline fall-back: **0.00**
(≠ 58.33) — degenerate, and the policy's own rule reads that zero as "where it comes to nothing **no
load is made**", i.e. the baseline instructs a reader not to perform the scored write at all
(**F-10**). `baseline.params` names `quarterly_allowance_amount`, `annual_allowance_amount` and
`enrollment_proration_basis`, none of which the baseline method reads, since it takes the period
allowance, the share and the ceiling all "as nothing" (**F-11**).
**Cross-difficulty:** `first_load_period_allowance` is the only one, and it discriminates nothing on
this world — both of its reachable tiers give 175.00 (**F-12**, demonstrated above). The other
product's rows it reads are seeded (`advantage_enrollments["cc7a06ec-…"]`).
**`first_load_ceiling` is inert in its own right:** tier 1 gives 700.00 and tier 2 would give
700.00 − 0.00 = 700.00; both leave `min(58.33, ceiling)` = 58.33. Only the artificial 0.00 baseline
moves the answer, so the ladder's own tiers are indistinguishable here.
**Stamp test:** no field names the outcome; the tiers rest on date arithmetic over
`program_start_date`, the `advantage` holding and a load count.
**Near-miss: none.** `initial_state` carries no `allowance_card_ledger` table at all, so every
history binding of this computation (`loads_already_made`, `loads_made_count`) is plainly zero and
nothing in the world is a record a careless reader would count and the rule exclude.

**Computation 2 — `catch_up_amount` (gold 408.34), 6 factors, 3 `method` + 3 `parameter`.**

| factor | effect | tier taken (evidence) | baseline | scored under baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `catch_up_periods_counted` | method | tier 1: quarters basis, one ledger entry after write 1 | `current_index` = 0 | **0.00** |
| `catch_up_first_period` | parameter | tier 1: `coverage_effective_date` 2026-05-01, after 1 January | `int(programme_start_months/period_months)` = 2 | **233.34** |
| `catch_up_first_period_share` | method | tier 1: cover began part way through Q2 | `period_months` = 3 | **466.67** |
| `catch_up_last_period` | method | tier 1: card in use, `months_open` 1 ≥ 1 | −1 | **0.00** |
| `catch_up_already_available` | parameter | tier 1: one load, nothing taken back | 0.00 | **466.67** |
| `catch_up_year_ceiling` | parameter | tier 1: 700.00 set and the plan in force | `loads_made` = 58.33 | **0.00** |

All six change the scored value. Whole-baseline fall-back: **0.00** (≠ 408.34) — degenerate, because
`baseline.rule` states in terms "The ceiling on the benefit year is taken as what has already been
made available, **so that nothing further is owed**" (**F-10**): the baseline of a catch-up policy
asserts there is nothing to catch up, and yields 0.00 on every world regardless of the records.
`baseline.params` names five keys the baseline reads none of (**F-11**).
**Cross-difficulty:** three factors — `catch_up_first_period` and `catch_up_first_period_share` read
`advantage_enrollments.coverage_effective_date`, and `catch_up_year_ceiling` reads the `advantage`
holding's status and (in its second tier) `XCOUNT` over `advantage_premium_ledger`. The holding and
the twelve ledger rows are seeded. `catch_up_first_period` and `catch_up_first_period_share` both
genuinely move the answer (233.34 and 466.67 against 408.34), so this task does carry a
weight-bearing cross-difficulty factor.
**Multi-source:** `catch_up_periods_counted` tier 1 conjoins a tier parameter (`benefit_period_basis`)
with a ledger fact (`ledger_entries >= 1`); `catch_up_year_ceiling` tier 1 conjoins a tier parameter
(`annual_allowance_amount`) with the `advantage` holding's status.
**Stamp test:** no field names the outcome.
**Near-miss: none that discriminates — `SOURCE-FACTOR` shortfall.** The only decoy rows in this
world are the six `advantage_premium_payment` entries a careless reader would add to the six
`advantage_premium_charge` entries when counting "the share of the year the medical plan was charged
for". But `plan_charged_months` appears **only in the second tier** of `catch_up_year_ceiling`, and
the tier taken is the first (the plan is in force), so the binding does not enter the result at all:
counting 12 instead of 6 leaves the scored value at 408.34. Recomputed and confirmed. Every other
factor's evidence in both computations is plainly present or plainly absent. Neither computation of
this task carries a record that a careless reader would count toward a tier and the rule excludes,
so both ladders are applied by inspection rather than by reading the rule.

**Counts for the task.** 10 factors over two computations, 4 and 6, each within 4–6, each with ≥ 2
`parameter` and ≥ 1 `method`. All ten pass the baseline-substitution test. Multi-source: present.
Cross-difficulty: present and weight-bearing in computation 2; present but non-discriminating in
computation 1 (**F-12**). Near-miss: **absent in both computations**.

## findings

**T1-1 — `SOURCE-CHAIN RED` — the customer names the prerequisite problem in his opening sentence.**
*Symptom:* the one prerequisite the task exists to make the agent discover is handed to the agent by
the caller before any record has been read.
*Root cause:* `user_scenario` gives the member two requests, one of which is the prerequisite problem
stated as an outcome.
*Evidence:* `tasks/1.json` → `user_scenario`, paragraph 1: *"A card came with my plan papers back in
September and I have not done a thing with it. **I would like to be able to use it at the chemist**,
and I want to know whether I am owed anything on it."* followed by "That is the whole of what he
wants, and he says it in the first half minute." The charter defines the transition the agent is
meant to find as exactly that state — `allowance.extended.yaml` → `lifecycle.transitions`,
`card_issued → active`, `by: user`: "The member activates the card and **the allowance becomes
spendable**." GT's own `design_rationale` states it plainly: "He asks two plain things: **to be able
to use it**, and whether anything is owed to him on it."
*Demonstrated consequence:* the prerequisite sentence
"The allowance owed for the benefit periods already gone is not made available before the card stands
in use on the programme record" is not needed to reach the gold write set or the gold order. An agent
that reads no policy at all still brings the card into use, because the caller asked for it; the
edge's discovery — which is the whole of what a one-edge tree tests — is supplied by the persona.
The edge's *weight* is intact (skipping the activation moves the catch-up from 408.34 to 0.00, and
that is verified above); what is not tested is that the agent had to find it.
*The author's counter-argument, weighed:* `design_rationale` answers that "Neither the amount he is
owed nor the reason he cannot yet be paid it is anywhere in what he says", i.e. that he names the two
outcomes but not the dependency between them. That is true, and the amount is genuinely hard. It does
not dispose of the criterion: the standard is whether the customer names a prerequisite outright,
because a prerequisite the customer has already asked for is no longer a problem the agent must find,
and with only two writes — one of them requested first by the caller and the other documented as
naming "the load that created it" (F-7) — the ordering that remains is close to forced. Contrast
task 0, where all three prerequisites appear only as reactions gated on the representative raising
them first.
*Affected artifact:* `tasks/1.json` → `user_scenario`, paragraph 1, against
`allowance.extended.yaml` → `allowance_ext_schedule_catch_up_load` → `prerequisite[0].policy_source`.
*Relation to previous revisions:* first revision.

**T1-2 — `SOURCE-TASK RED` — the catch-up load's `benefit_period` is not entailed by any rule
sentence; GT's uniqueness argument rests on a principle the charter does not state.**
*Symptom:* a scored argument with three defensible values and no charter sentence excluding two of
them.
*Root cause:* `allowance_ext_schedule_catch_up_load`'s `rule` fixes the amount, the load it names and
the ceiling, but never says which benefit period the extra load is placed in, and its `compute` binds
no period label.
*Evidence:* the policy's full `rule` block contains no sentence about the period the extra load
carries (searched term by term); `post_catch_up_load_838eeda2` nevertheless requires
`benefit_period` as a fixed-format argument. GT's
`evaluation_criteria[9].argument_uniqueness_tracing.benefit_period` grounds `2026-Q4` on "an extra
load is placed in the benefit period **it is made available in**" — a sentence that appears nowhere
in this policy, in its `base_policy_refs` (`allowance_load_schedule`,
`allowance_agg_combined_annual_cap`), or anywhere else in the charter.
*Demonstrated consequence:* the competing readings are live and the charter supports them at least as
well. Base `allowance_rollover_and_expiry` states the opposite principle in terms — "An allowance
**belongs to the benefit period it was loaded for**" — which points at `2026-Q2`, the first period the
allowance is owed for. And this difficulty's other two period-carrying writes both follow the
"period the money relates to" convention rather than "the period it is made available in": task 0's
recovery credit is made available on 2026-10-12 (Q4) and placed in `2026-Q3` because that is the
period the transaction it relates to belonged to, and **this task's own first load** is made
available on 2026-10-20 (Q4) and placed in `2026-Q3` because that is the period the programme opened
in. A reader who carries the convention the other two writes of this difficulty use arrives at
`2026-Q3` or `2026-Q2`, not `2026-Q4`. The choice is not cosmetic: a catch-up placed in `2026-Q2` or
`2026-Q3` lands in a period `allowance_ext_period_end_expiry` would treat as already dying, and one
placed in `2026-Q4` does not. "GT chose this one" is not exclusion evidence.
*Affected artifact:* `allowance.extended.yaml` → `allowance_ext_schedule_catch_up_load` → `rule`,
`compute`; `task_tools.py` → `post_catch_up_load_838eeda2` → `benefit_period`; scored item
`evaluation_criteria[9].arguments.benefit_period`.
*Relation to previous revisions:* first revision.

**T1-3 — `SOURCE-FACTOR RED` — the task's only cross-difficulty factor on the first-load computation
discriminates nothing, and its fall-through is unreachable.**
*Symptom:* an agent that never opens the medical plan's record scores the first load correctly.
*Root cause:* `first_load_period_allowance`'s two reachable tiers select the same number on this
world, and its third tier describes a customer this write cannot have.
*Evidence:* tier 1 is "the quarterly allowance that medical plan tier carries" —
`advantage_enrollments["cc7a06ec-…"].variant_name = "Ridgecrest Advantage Signature (PPO)"` →
`otc_allowance_quarterly: 175.0` in `blueprint/products/advantage.yaml`. Tier 2 is "the card's own
tier quarterly allowance" — `allowance_programs["7bc19e7a-…"].variant_name = "Ridgecrest Healthy
Options Card - Premier"` → `quarterly_allowance_amount: 175.0`. Tier 3 is "otherwise: nothing",
reached only when the card hangs on no in-force medical plan, which base
`allowance_programme_opening` forbids ("An allowance programme is opened only alongside a health plan
enrollment whose tier carries an allowance") and base `allowance_health_plan_tier_interaction`
repeats ("A member holding a stand-alone Part D drug plan and no medical plan holds no allowance card
at all").
*Demonstrated consequence:* recomputed with `period_allowance` forced to tier 2 — the card's own
175.00, requiring no cross-product read at all — the scored `first_load_amount` is **58.33**,
identical to gold. The factor's ladder therefore has one reachable outcome on this world, and the
only thing that moves the scored value is the 0.00 baseline, which is tier 3, the tier no customer
reaching this write can be on. This is the sole cross-difficulty factor of the `first_load_amount`
computation.
*Affected artifact:* `allowance.extended.yaml` →
`allowance_ext_card_in_use_first_load.factors[first_load_period_allowance]`;
`tasks/1.json` → `initial_state.advantage_enrollments.cc7a06ec-…`.
*Also on this computation:* `first_load_ceiling` is inert in the same way — tier 1 gives 700.00 and
tier 2 would give 700.00 − 0.00 = 700.00, and `min(58.33, ceiling)` is 58.33 either way; only the
0.00 baseline moves the answer, and that baseline is again an unreachable tier
(`annual_allowance_amount <= 0`, while all six card tiers publish 180.0 or more).
*Relation to previous revisions:* first revision.

**T1-4 — `SOURCE-FACTOR RED` — neither computation carries a near-miss, and both baselines are
degenerate.**
*Symptom:* every factor's evidence is plainly present or plainly absent, and the fall-back number is
a constant zero the policies read as "make no entry".
*Evidence, near-miss:* `initial_state` carries no `allowance_card_ledger` table at all, so every
history binding of the first computation is plainly nil. The only decoy rows anywhere in the world
are the six `advantage_premium_payment` entries a careless reader would add to the six
`advantage_premium_charge` entries when counting the months the plan was charged for — but
`plan_charged_months` appears **only in the second tier** of `catch_up_year_ceiling`, and the tier
taken is the first (the plan is in force). Recomputed with `plan_charged_months` forced to 12: the
scored `catch_up_amount` is **408.34**, unchanged. The decoy cannot change the score, so it is not a
near-miss.
*Evidence, baselines:* whole-baseline fall-backs are **0.00** on both computations (GT's
`baseline_result` agrees). `allowance_ext_card_in_use_first_load`'s baseline takes the period
allowance, the share owed and the ceiling all "as nothing" and its rule reads the result as "where it
comes to nothing **no load is made**"; `allowance_ext_schedule_catch_up_load`'s baseline states "The
ceiling on the benefit year is taken as what has already been made available, **so that nothing
further is owed**", which returns 0.00 on every world whatever the records say. The standard first
load a card publishes is its tier's `quarterly_allowance_amount` — 175.0 for Premier, a figure the
charter carries for all six tiers — so a baseline of nothing is a zero where the standard method
plainly gives a figure. GT's own `design_rationale` states the effect without treating it as a
defect: "an agent who reads only the computation documents and none of the factor documents computes
**nothing at all on either write**". A baseline is required to yield a definite wrong *number*; these
yield a refusal, and the tools reject a non-positive amount, so a reader following either baseline
makes no call.
*Affected artifact:* `allowance.extended.yaml` → the `baseline.rule` blocks of both policies; see
`_difficulty.md` → `findings` → F-10 and F-12 for the charter-global form.
*Relation to previous revisions:* first revision.

**T1-5 — observation — F-6, F-7 and F-8 bear on this task.**
Both of this task's policies carry an **empty `compute_basis`** (F-6), so the rule/compute
correspondence is asserted for none of their 18 bindings. The `post_catch_up_load_838eeda2` docstring
sources its `source_ledger_entry_id` from "the confirmation of the load that created it" (F-7),
which on this world can only be the activation call, reinforcing the ordering T1-1 already gives
away — GT's own `argument_uniqueness_tracing` for that argument quotes the phrase as its basis. Edge
E4's declared `effect` ends "lowering the allowance still owed" (F-8) while
`prerequisite_closure.edges[0].unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by` records the opposite in
the same file — "the allowance still owed is then **408.34 rather than nothing**". Recomputed: 0.00
without the activation, 408.34 with it.
*Relation to previous revisions:* first revision.

**T1-6 — observation — the seeded programme start contradicts base `allowance_programme_opening`.**
*Evidence:* `allowance_programs["7bc19e7a-…"].program_start_date = "2026-09-01"` against
`advantage_enrollments["cc7a06ec-…"].coverage_effective_date = "2026-05-01"`; base
`allowance_programme_opening`: "The programme runs for the benefit year of the health plan that
carries it, **starts on the health plan's coverage effective date**, and can never start before it."
*Consequence:* none on the score — a solver takes the programme record as authoritative, and the gap
is the very fact the catch-up policy exists to remedy. Recorded because the extended remedy rests on
a world its own base policy says cannot arise.
*Relation to previous revisions:* first revision.

### problem_chain (revision 2)

Root unchanged: `allowance_ext_schedule_catch_up_load`. One prerequisite sentence, verbatim in the
root's own rule and unchanged by the rework: *"The allowance owed for the benefit periods already
gone is not made available before the card stands in use on the programme record."*

**Edge → `allowance_ext_card_in_use_first_load`.** False at the opening:
`allowance_programs["7bc19e7a-…"]` carries `card_activated_date: ""`, `status: "card_issued"` and
`current_balance: "0.00"`, and no ledger row belongs to that programme. Resolved by
`activate_allowance_card_a5740baf` (`owner=user`), the only write of this difficulty that sets
`card_activated_date`. **Load-bearing:** skip it and the catch-up computes to **0.00** instead of
583.34. n = 1, one `value_input` edge (floor 1 met), no cycle, one `owner=user` write. Tool bodies
re-read: neither judges the prerequisite.

**T1-1 verified closed — the persona no longer names the prerequisite.** The opening is now a single
request: *"A card came with my plan papers back in September and nobody has told me what it is for.
**I want to know whether I am owed anything on it.**"* — followed, in the same paragraph, by an
explicit disclaimer that the round-1 version lacked: *"He does not ask for anything to be done to the
card and would not know what to ask for; he is content for the plan to do whatever its own side of
the work is."* The round-1 clause "I would like to be able to use it at the chemist", which stated
the prerequisite problem in plain business words, is **gone**.

The reaction does not smuggle it back in. Every mention of bringing the card into use is now behind
the representative: *"**If** the representative explains that bringing the card into use is something
only he can do and hands it over to him, he does it there and then"*; *"**If** the representative
tells him that something has to be put right on the card's record before anything can be put on it,
he says to go ahead"* — the second names no act and supplies no route, and both are conditioned on
the representative having raised the matter first. Even holding the card is elicited: *"**Asked**
whether he has the card itself, he says it is here on the table and reads the last four digits."* The
closing line was rewritten too — round 1 had him told "that the card is in use", presupposing he had
asked for it; round 2 has him told only "what has been put on the card for the periods gone by". His
parting remark that he will try it at the chemist in the morning follows the work rather than
requesting it.

So the agent must now derive the hop itself: read the programme record, find the card has never been
brought into use, read the root policy's prerequisite sentence, and discover that the allowance owed
waits on that state — none of which the caller supplies. **The edge is discovered from the policy,
not handed over by the persona.**

`baseline.rule` states, and 250.00 is one benefit period's allowance. **F-10 is closed for both of
this task's computations** (round 1: 0.00 and 0.00, each read by its own rule as "no load is made" /
"nothing further is owed").

**T1-3 verified closed — the cross-difficulty factor now discriminates.** The rework closed it by
changing the medical plan tier, and the change does what it claims:

**T1-4 verified closed — the added 2025 programme is a genuine near-miss.** Recomputed:

- counting its 30.50 forfeiture as an allowance taken back gives **523.84**;
- computing the first load on the 2025 Core programme instead of the 2026 Premier one gives

The rule excludes it three times over — the entries belong to another `allowance_program_id`, the
programme is `closed`, and it is a 2025 benefit year — and a careless reader who sums the member's
card history across programmes lands on a different number. The `first_load_amount` computation reads
no ledger history at all, so its near-miss is the wrong-programme trap above.

The round-1 decoy is **still inert**, and it is worth saying so plainly: forcing `plan_charged_months`
from 6 to 11 (a reader adding the five `advantage_premium_payment` rows to the six charges) leaves

`catch_up_year_ceiling` and the tier taken is the first. The finding is closed by the new record, not
by that one.
